core_obligations: Initial step (proof lines 2160-2176): using hypothesis (1), the author observes that the relevant cohomology groups H^p(h_U^#, g^{-1}I) vanish, which is the starting point of the induction.

Induction hypothesis and step (proof lines 2179-2196): the author proves by induction on n that hypotheses (1) and (2) imply the exactness of the extended Cech complexes up to degree n, writing the induction hypothesis IH_n and deducing IH_{n+1} from the long exact sequences obtained from a surjection of sheaves of sets.
proof_roadmap: Start from the vanishing of cohomology given by hypothesis (1).
Formulate the induction hypothesis that the extended Cech complexes are exact up to degree n.
Deduce the next degree from the long exact sequences attached to a surjection of sheaves of sets.
Conclude total acyclicity, and note the converse.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises total acyclicity of an abelian sheaf on a site by two conditions: the vanishing of its cohomology on all objects, and the exactness of the extended Cech complexes associated to every surjection of sheaves of sets (statement lines 2144-2158). The proof is an induction on the degree of exactness: the vanishing in hypothesis (1) provides the initial case (proof lines 2160-2176), and the induction hypothesis IH_n is stepped up using the long exact sequences obtained from a surjection of sheaves of sets (proof lines 2179-2196). The non-formal content is the induction over the extended Cech complex. The claim is H2: one induction with a clearly stated hypothesis.
